claim_boundary: Eight assignments are analyst-reviewed from captured official PDFs and structured notes; claims are not independent reproductions.

rows.title: Frequency-Domain Enhanced Extreme Bandwidth Extension Network with ICCRN for Superior Speech Quality
rows.semantic_reasoning: Frequency-domain bandwidth extension reconstructs missing high-frequency structure under perceptual and signal constraints.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Bandwidth extension must recreate missing high-frequency speech without inventing spectral detail that listeners hear as distortion. Mechanism: The model operates on frequency representations, combines local and global context, and is compared against EBEN and other bandwidth-extension baselines. Result: The tests show gains over the original EBEN, including a 40-person MUSHRA comparison; the authors report clearer high-frequency detail and less distortion. Boundary: French LibriSpeech, sampling setup, listeners, and author-reported metrics bound the result; other languages remain open.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: MiSTR: Multi-Modal iEEG-to-Speech Synthesis with Transformer-Based Prosody Prediction and Neural Phase Reconstruction
rows.semantic_reasoning: Neural-signal speech reconstruction separates content/prosody prediction from waveform phase reconstruction.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Brain recordings may contain enough motor or auditory information to reconstruct intelligible speech for people who cannot produce it normally. Mechanism: MiSTR uses a multimodal iEEG encoder, Transformer spectrogram/prosody prediction, and a neural phase vocoder with adaptive spectral correction. Result: The paper reports higher fidelity and naturalness than listed baselines and MOSA 3.38. Boundary: Dataset, subjects, protocol, learned evaluator, and paper-reported comparisons limit clinical claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Domain Adaptation Method and Modality Gap Impact in Audio-Text Models for Prototypical Sound Classification
rows.semantic_reasoning: Audio-side adaptation tests whether an audio-text representation preserves open-vocabulary labels across acoustic domains.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Audio-text classifiers fail when the acoustic domain changes even if the label vocabulary stays fixed. Mechanism: The method aligns audio representations to the target domain and compares audio-based with text-based adaptation. Result: Audio-based adaptation gives the largest reported gains across tested conditions. Boundary: Sound set, target examples, class construction, and reported accuracy limit open-world claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Coping with segmental–prosodic incongruity in spoken word recognition in Japanese
rows.semantic_reasoning: Controlled incongruity experiments test how lexical pitch accent and segments jointly shape word recognition.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Listeners combine segmental sounds and lexical pitch accent when recognizing Japanese words, even when the cues disagree. Mechanism: Experiments isolate cue type, delay, and lexical repetition; mixed-effects models compare segmental and prosodic conditions. Result: Results suggest prosodic mispronunciation inhibits recognition at the tested delay. Boundary: Japanese materials, pitch-accent system, participants, and laboratory task limit cross-language generalization.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Facilitating Personalized TTS for Dysarthric Speakers Using Knowledge Anchoring and Curriculum Learning
rows.semantic_reasoning: Teacher anchoring and curriculum learning adapt TTS to dysarthric speakers while separating identity retention from intelligibility.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Personalized TTS for dysarthric speakers must preserve identity while producing intelligible speech from scarce and errorful recordings. Mechanism: A teacher-student knowledge-anchoring framework is evaluated across speaker groups with shortened audio. Result: Curriculum and anchoring lower PER and improve speaker similarity across reported groups. Boundary: Groups, language, recording conditions, and reported metrics limit clinical claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Hearing deficits of transformer-based ASR for anechoic and spatial signals
rows.semantic_reasoning: Speech-reception thresholds compare ASR and human recognition under hearing-relevant noise and spatial conditions.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: ASR and humans should be compared on the same speech-in-noise task rather than assuming low WER means human-like hearing. Mechanism: Whisper models are tested on anechoic and spatial signals; thresholds come from WER curves at 50% error. Result: Model size improves ASR thresholds, but the gap changes with language, room, and spatial signals. Boundary: Whisper versions, German/English material, steady noise, and laboratory setup limit claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: TalTech Systems for the Interspeech 2025 ML-SUPERB 2.0 Challenge
rows.semantic_reasoning: Language identification and specialized multilingual decoding allocate recognition capacity across languages.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A multilingual recognizer must allocate limited capacity across languages with different data sizes and acoustic demands. Mechanism: The system combines language identification with multilingual ASR and customized models, then evaluates language ID and CER. Result: The system is competitive with challenge baselines and identifies languages needing targeted work. Boundary: Challenge data, language mix, averaging, and tuning limit all-multilingual claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Evaluating ASR Robustness to Spontaneous Speech Errors: A Study of WhisperX Using a Speech Error Database
rows.semantic_reasoning: Annotated spontaneous speech errors map where ASR crosses failure boundaries by error type and position.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: ASR robustness should be tested on errors people actually produce, not only clean speech or synthetic noise. Mechanism: The study evaluates sound and word errors with controlled classification variables and compares initial, medial, and final positions. Result: Sound errors have higher transcription accuracy than word errors, with position-dependent differences. Boundary: Database, annotations, WhisperX, language, and task design limit generalization.
